makingOf.title: How Saqi is built
makingOf.intro: Five short scenes: one look on every screen, the water maths, how each decision explains itself, how every update is checked, and who made it.

scene1.title: One look, everywhere.
scene1.body: Saqi uses one shared set of colours, sizes and motions, so every screen looks and moves the same way. The dry-to-wet water scale is the same seven colours wherever you meet it: on the map, in the plan and on the phone.
scene1.caption: Seven colours for the water left in the soil, from dry to wet. The map paints every block with them.

scene2.title: Water first.
scene2.body: Saqi waters a block only when what the crop drinks tomorrow would take the soil below its safe level, and then only back up to its target. Here is the whole sum for D-1, the Khalas date palms, on a day when the weather draws 5.8 mm of water from the ground.
scene2.note: Nothing is rounded until it’s shown to you.

terms.taw: Water the root zone can hold, mm
terms.efficiency: How efficiently water reaches the roots
terms.wetted: Share of the ground the drippers wet

scene3.title: Every decision explains itself.
scene3.body: No black box. Every recommendation comes with the reasons behind it, in the order Saqi weighed them. These three are exactly what Saqi decided for Farm 07.

scene4.title: Checked before every update.
scene4.body: Every calculation and every screen is checked automatically before each update goes live. These are the checks that run each time.

scene5.title: Built by Husni Ramdani.
scene5.body: Built for a farm that doesn’t exist yet, to show how I’d build for one that does.

instruments.title: Small instruments, honest numbers.
instruments.lead: Every figure shows its unit, its source and its age. Nothing on screen is decoration. If it moves, water moved.

instruments.footnote: These figures are an example night on the fictional Farm 07, with ET₀ at 5.8 mm tomorrow. In the app, weather and ET₀ come live from Open-Meteo and every soil reading is simulated. The app says so wherever they appear.
